correctness.rationale: The normal form is correct as stated. At a lax disjunction the two sets of rows satisfying the child flattenings cover the parent and realize each of the respective guarded obligations; the forward direction uses any witnessing split. Intersecting the ambient team with the root flattening preserves witnesses from any feasible subteam and gives the greatest one. Each guard is a conjunction of at most the formula depth many flattenings and there is at most one per NE occurrence. Input offsets, nested-parenthesis counts, row/column indices and recomputed Boolean formula value suffice for deterministic logspace; a singleton classical team gives the usual Boolean formula-value hardness. The empty team and infeasibility are handled correctly; a singleton satisfies NE ∨ NE only under lax, not strict, splitting. Independent check: `python3 /workspace/branches/independent_examples.py 4` compared possible-row propagation to unrestricted lax splits on 45,584 formula/team pairs and checked greatest subteams; finite evidence only.

evidence: From (1), S⊆U can only satisfy inside M=U∩F_root. Any witnesses in S persist in M, so M is the greatest satisfying subteam if any one exists.

In the comparison's representation, the obligation for an NE occurrence at the root is the intersection of the sibling supports at its conjunction ancestors. On any row, check those support formulas sequentially by walking the ancestor chain and evaluating each sibling with NE replaced by top. A scan for a passing row for each obligation, and a scan for root-support membership, use O(log N) space exactly as for the frozen guard encoding.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The stronger implication is from the exact per-occurrence recursion, not from the stated running time or fixed-point cutoff alone. The two resulting logarithmic-space procedures differ just in how the already proved support restrictions are presented. The classical singleton lower bound is standard; no distinct claim survives this comparison.

evidence: Equation (1) of the comparison record is S⊆F_u and S∩W≠∅ for each W, with F_u exactly the truth set of the NE→top flattening. It has one obligation per NE occurrence before removing duplicates and uses the same canonical overlapping split.

The comparison propagates obligations by intersecting with the sibling support at a conjunction and leaving them alone at disjunction. If obligations are tagged by their generating occurrence, at each node its obligation is exactly the frozen guard intersected with that node's F_u: at conjunction this introduces the sibling support, and at disjunction it is redundant since the child obligation is already in the child support.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The recursive rules are two representations of the same witness predicates on root-flat rows. Finite-variable restriction is no difference: projection to the finitely many formula variables preserves satisfaction, since split witnesses project and projected splits pull back.

Its representation mechanically yields the greatest-subteam conclusion and the deterministic logspace upper bound, not merely a polynomial-time conclusion. This is a finding of mathematical coverage in the available corpus, not a priority or dependence assertion; the compared record's displayed catalogue date is later.
